title: In 53 epilepsy patients, group tractography did not improve held-out prediction of interictal iEEG coupling beyond distance and channel effects, but group fMRI FC added 0.012 R²
abstract: Question: does group diffusion-MRI wiring predict resting human iEEG coupling between channel pairs after geometry and per-channel effects, and is any gain specific to the real wiring? This separates two explanations of earlier campaign results (no wiring signal in fMRI FC; a small specific signal in causal CCEP responses). Data: OpenNeuro ds004100 v1.1.3 (HUP, CC0), two separate 300-s interictal clips in each of 53 patients (35 SEEG, 18 ECoG); 3,095 grey-matter bipolar channels outside seizure-onset and resection zones; 98,543 pairs. Wiring: HCP group connectome (ENIGMA, Schaefer-400). Method: plan hashed before analysis; orthogonalised amplitude envelope correlation (AEC-orth, primary), wPLI and coherence in six bands; within-patient ridge models fitted on one clip and scored on held-out pairs of the other clip; 20 degree/length-preserving and 20 distance-bin surrogate connectomes. Results: the pre-registered test failed. Direct wiring changed held-out R² by -0.0021 (95% CI -0.0049 to +0.0002); no band, measure or robustness variant gave a positive gain. Post hoc, with rank-normalised coupling, geometry and channel effects gave R² 0.13 (cross-clip) and 0.32 (same clip), and wiring still added about zero (-0.0009; +0.0004). Real wiring beat all surrogates and row-permuted wiring by 0.002-0.003 R² (CI excludes 0), about the cost of fitting two columns and about 1% of the reliable pair-specific coupling. Group fMRI FC added +0.012 R², above all distance-matched shuffles. Limitations: group wiring, coarse parcels, 300-s clips, epilepsy patients; the informative rank-normalised tests are post hoc.

display.caption: Gain in held-out R² (x 1000) from direct wiring after geometry and channel effects, AEC-orth, per band and band mean, 53 patients. Blue: real wiring with 95% patient-bootstrap CI. Grey: 20 rewired connectomes. Yellow: 20 distance-bin shuffles. Red crosses: row-permuted real wiring. A: pre-registered raw cross-clip score. B: post hoc rank-normalised cross-clip score.

A: raw AEC-orth against distance for pairs with and without a direct tract. B: clip-to-clip reliability of pair coupling, raw and after geometry and channel effects. C: held-out R² of the model ladder in three scoring schemes.
Direct-wiring gains in all pre-registered and post hoc variants, real-minus-permuted gains and the group fMRI FC comparator (x 1000 held-out R², 95% CI); grey bar = largest surrogate or shuffle gain.

citations.reason: CCEP test of group tractography with the same connectome, surrogate code (features.py, unchanged) and design; we compare its small specific gain with resting iEEG coupling.
Found almost no pair-specific wiring signal in FC after node controls; our iEEG result agrees in electrophysiology.
Calibrated surrogate tests; human wiring gains did not exceed geometry-only gains; our result is consistent.
Multi-step communication measures add little FC variance beyond direct wiring and geometry; we test the same measures on iEEG.
Earlier strength- and distance-matched surrogate wiring test of FC.
